title: Chasoñ: Supporting Cross HBM Channel Data Migration to Enable Efficient Sparse Algebraic Acceleration
problem: HBM-based sparse accelerators suffer from high resource underutilization due to static non-zero scheduling that cannot redistribute work across HBM channels when data access patterns are irregular. Existing designs like Serpens fix data-to-channel mapping, leaving processing elements idle when a channel has no work.
motivation: Sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV) is memory-bound and irregular; HBM's multiple independent channels are underutilized with static scheduling, capping throughput well below hardware limits.
method: Chaso is an FPGA-based streaming HBM accelerator for SpMV that introduces Cross-HBM Channel out-of-Order Scheduling (CrHCS), which dynamically migrates non-zero data across HBM channels at runtime to balance load. When one channel's processing elements are starved, CrHCS identifies data in other channels and migrates it, enabling out-of-order execution across channel boundaries. The design is implemented on AMD Alveo U55C running at 301 MHz, targeting the SuiteSparse and SNAP matrix collections.
key_novelty: CrHCS is the first non-zero scheduling scheme that permits out-of-order cross-channel data migration in HBM-based sparse accelerators, directly addressing per-channel load imbalance.
contributions: Cross-HBM Channel out-of-Order Scheduling (CrHCS) for dynamic non-zero load balancing across HBM channels
Chaso HBM streaming accelerator design implemented on AMD Alveo U55C at 301 MHz
Up to 8x throughput improvement and 2.03x energy efficiency gain over Serpens baseline
Open-source implementation demonstrating generality across SuiteSparse and SNAP benchmarks

metrics.speedup: up to 8x over Serpens, 20.33x over RTX 4090, 11.65x over RTX 6000 Ada, 2.67x over Core i9-11980HK

limitations: Evaluation is limited to SpMV; generalization of CrHCS to other sparse kernels (e.g., SpGEMM) is not demonstrated.
primary_theme: HBM-aware dynamic scheduling for sparse linear algebra acceleration
